title: Blaze: Fully Featured Ledger Emulator, Transaction Builder for the Chang Hard Fork and PlutusV3

・Detailed issue tracking and iterative planning which describes all required emulator features for Chang hard fork and PlutusV3 support, made public
・Technical analysis on current implementations via the cardano node, other transaction builders (CML, Lucid, e.t.c.)
・Performance benchmarks and testing criteria
ms.criteria:
・Proposed feature set covers all aspects of Chang hard fork and PlutusV3 capabilities
・Technical analysis provides actionable insights for emulator development
・Performance benchmarks are realistic and aligned with production node requirements

ms.report:
A. Output: Functional prototype of core emulator features in TypeScript.
Acceptance criteria: The emulator can simulate block production and transaction processing.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m2.md#implementation-evidence — block and transaction simulation is implemented by stepForwardBlock, stepForwardToSlot, submitTransaction, and awaitTransactionConfirmation in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/src/emulator.ts
B. Output: Initial support for Chang governance features.
Acceptance criteria: Basic Chang governance features (voting, proposal submission) are functional.
Evidence: Governance state and epoch-boundary processing live in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/tree/main/packages/blaze-emulator/src/governance. Proposal submission, DRep voting, ratification, and enactment are tested in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/test/Governance.test.ts
C. Output: Basic PlutusV3 capabilities integration.
Acceptance criteria: PlutusV3 scripts can be executed in the emulator environment.
Evidence: PlutusV3 witness handling in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/src/emulator.ts. The governance tests execute compiled PlutusV3 scripts for script DRep voting and proposal-policy redeemers, built from the Aiken fixtures in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/test/aiken/plutus.ts
D. Output: Unit test suite for core components, with CI logs and a coverage report.
Acceptance criteria: Unit tests cover at least 80% of core functionality, CI logs show them passing, and a coverage report shows 80%+.
Evidence: 5 test files, 55 tests, 82.9% statement coverage from bun --filter @blaze-cardano/emulator coverage. Results table: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m2.md#verification. CI logs

ms.report:
A. Output: Full implementation of Chang governance mechanisms.
Acceptance criteria: The emulator supports DRep registration and delegation, proposal submission and tracking, voting, Constitutional Committee state, ratification, enactment, expiry, deposit refunds, treasury effects, constitutions, committee updates, and no-confidence actions.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m3.md#implementation-evidence and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/test/Governance.test.ts
B. Output: Comprehensive PlutusV3 support.
Acceptance criteria: Non-trivial PlutusV3 scripts can participate in governance as script-managed DReps and proposal-policy scripts. Valid redeemers are accepted and invalid redeemers are rejected.
Evidence: The Aiken validator is at https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/test/aiken/validators/governance.ak and the generated typed scripts are at https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-emulator/test/aiken/plutus.ts. The reproducible example is at https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/governance-demo.ts. Video walkthrough: https://youtu.be/60jULudi7NI
C. Output: Tooling for creating and managing test governance scenarios.
Acceptance criteria: Developers can create deterministic governance states, advance blocks and epochs, inspect proposals, and reproduce script-managed governance flows.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m3.md#implementation-evidence and https://blaze.butane.dev/emulator/guides/governance-testing
D. Output: Enhanced transaction builder for the new Chang transaction types.
Acceptance criteria: The transaction builder supports DRep registration, update and unregistration, vote delegation, governance proposals and votes, and governance script redeemers.
Evidence: https://github.c

ms.promise:
・REST API server which mimics common endpoints for users to submit and query a remote emulator
・Support for different network configurations (mainnet, testnet, custom)
・Comprehensive documentation and usage examples
・Compatibility with different transaction builders (i.e., can build transactions in Haskell, submit them to the Blaze emulator in typescript by transferring script CBOR)
ms.criteria:
・A live server is functioning and usable
・The emulator boasts better configuration with regards to the chain network, timing settings (i.e. slot length, block length)
・Full endpoint and user documentation is available at https://blaze.butane.dev
・The emulator is independent of Blaze's transaction building
・Emulator performance meets or exceeds predefined benchmarks
ms.report:
A. Output: A REST API server with endpoints for submitting transactions to a remote emulator and querying its state.
Acceptance criteria: The standalone server starts successfully and exposes health, configuration, wallet, transaction, state, OpenAPI, and Swagger endpoints. Its operation is demonstrated through a real HTTP listener and covered by integration tests.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m4.md#a-rest-api-server and https://blaze.butane.dev/emulator/guides/rpc-server/
B. Output: Support for mainnet, testnet, and custom emulator network configurations.
Acceptance criteria: The emulator supports mainnet, preprod, preview, SanchoNet, and custom chain IDs. Slot length, slots per block, slots per epoch, and protocol parameters can be configured and inspected through the API. Tests cover the presets and overrides.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m4.md#b-network-configuration
C. Output: Comprehensive endpoint documentation and usage examples.
Acceptance criteria: The published documentation covers server startup, health and clock queries, network configuration, wallet setup, raw CBOR submission, script publishing, governance data, OpenAPI access, Swagger UI, and cleanup.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200040/m4.md#c-documentation-and-examples and https://blaze.butane.dev/emulator/guides/rpc-server/
D. Output: Compatibility with transactions produced by different transaction-building tools.
Acceptance criteria: The HTTP endpoint accepts signed transaction CBOR without depending on Blaze TxBuilder. The integration test constructs and signs a transaction with lower-level Cardano serialization types, submits it through the HTTP API, advances the emulator, and verifies the resulting outputs. The current benchmark run meets or exceeds the M1 baseline for all three original scenarios.
Evidence: https://gith
